Subject: Crestline activation exception — per-tenant compliance export

Team,

Quick context: Crestline (large regional bank) is at signature but their procurement + compliance team requires an isolated export of inference traces per tenant for their audit controls. It's a gating item for their production activation. HubSpot shows $1.8M ARR commit if we go live this quarter (DL-2026-0987). I attached the requirements spreadsheet and their proposed SLA.

Ask: sales needs an internal commitment window and a minimally viable scope we can promise to Crestline. Specifically: can Eng ship a scoped, non-prod pilot (tenant-level export to an S3 bucket per customer, redacted) within 3 weeks from a sprint start? If not, what is the fastest mitigation we can offer (example: scheduled manual exports + contractual audit support)?

Constraints we have from the customer:
- Exports must include token-level latency traces, call IDs, and prompt/response hashes (they allow hashed content)
- Per-tenant isolation (Crestline wants separate objects and retention policy)
- Auditability for SOC2 scope

I realize this is ask-for-exception territory vs. roadmap — happy to discuss tradeoffs. Ben, can you please include the timeline they're expecting in the LOE conversation?

Thanks,
Grace

--
Grace O'Connor

Subject: Re: Crestline activation exception — per-tenant compliance export

Thanks for the context, Grace. I pulled the attachments — good summary. A few clarifying questions before we triage this to ENG backlog:

1) When you say "token-level latency traces" — do they need the full token stream or aggregates (per-request latency, token count, timestamps)? Full token stream has privacy implications even if hashed.
2) For "separate objects and retention" — is the retention per-tenant variable or a single retention policy with export segregation?
3) Is Crestline willing to accept an initial POC that excludes full KV cache dumps (only request/response metadata + hashes)?

From product perspective, assuming we avoid exporting raw content, the minimal viable export surface is: request metadata (ids, timestamps), response metadata, hashes, and a per-tenant manifest. Hooking that into our export pipeline is ~2–3 sprints of work including: schema, export interface, auth/iam binding, and S3 per-tenant prefix enforcement. That's a ballpark; Jasmine, can you confirm engineering feasibility and whether a 3-week sprint pilot is realistic if we scope down?

If speed is critical, we should consider a runbook + manual export service for the first 60 days post-signature while we deliver automated exports. That's lower risk for data but higher operational lift.

- Soojin

--
Soojin Lee
Group Product Manager, Platform
Redwood Inference
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 14:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Crestline activation exception — per-tenant compliance export

Soojin / Grace — quick engineering take after a 30-min sync with infra:

- Full token streams (even if hashed) require additional PII review and would likely push this out because of redaction proofing and storage encryption requirements. Not ideal for a fast pilot.
- We can ship a scoped pilot in 3 weeks if the scope is strictly: request/response metadata + per-request hashes + callIDs. That means no KV cache dumps, no token-by-token export, and a standard retention policy (e.g., 90 days) on S3 prefixes per tenant. Work items:
  1) small export service + auth binding to customer S3 (1 week core dev)
  2) per-tenant prefix enforcement and retention policy wiring (3 days)
  3) logging/audit trail + access matrix proof (3 days)
  4) test matrix and dry run with internal tenant (2 days)

We'll need a prioritized ticket in the ENG triage board and an explicit canary plan. Also call out the risk: the manual export fallback is doable but will require the CS/Field Ops team to manage exports daily until automation lands.

If product signs off on the scoping decision (no token streams, 90d retention), engineering can commit to a POC deploy to staging in ~3 weeks. Otherwise timeline slips to 6+ weeks.

-Jasmine

--
Jasmine Liu

Redwood Inference

Adding customer urgency: Crestline is asking for production activation by July 12th. Legal has a few doc edits but compliance is the blocker. If we can promise a 3-week scoped POC (staging) with follow-up automated export in 60 days, they're likely to accept that for signature and start the payment terms. I can push for the manual-export SLA in contract language for the first 60 days.

Two asks for the group:
- Product: confirm scope (Soojin, pls reply with an explicit "scope approved" so I can lock language in the LOE)
- Eng: if Jasmine's plan is feasible, can we get a rough calendar (start date, milestones) so I can coordinate procurement and legal with dates?

Ben

Jasmine — please file ENG-3412 with the work breakdown above and ping me when you have sprint assignment + tentative start date. Ben — I'll share the acceptance criteria doc for contract language. Grace — I'll join the customer call on Friday if helpful.

Thanks all — let's get this moving.
